options.name: Java 21 + Spring Boot 3 + Maven + SQLite
options.test_framework: JUnit 5 with Spring Boot Test (MockMvc / TestRestTemplate)
pros: Only stack marked VALIDATED end-to-end in the orchestrator, which lowers delivery risk
Spring Web MVC handles the needed status codes directly: ResponseEntity with 302 plus a Location header (FR-2, FR-3), 404 for unknown codes (FR-12) and 4xx for validation failures (FR-10)
java.net.URI makes it simple to accept only absolute http/https URLs (FR-10)
An atomic SQL UPDATE (clicks = clicks + 1, last_click_at = now) gives exactly-once counting per successful redirect (FR-5, FR-6, FR-14)
HTTP-level tests that do not follow redirects map directly onto every acceptance criterion (AC-1.1 to AC-15.1)
No Spring Security dependency is needed, so all endpoints stay unauthenticated (FR-15)
cons: More verbose and slower to start than the Python or Go options
Spring Boot is heavier than this small service strictly needs
SQLite serializes writes, so concurrent redirect increments are serialized. This is acceptable because the spec has no throughput NFR.
options.fit: Strong fit. It covers all MVP FRs (FR-1 to FR-15) with a single short_link table (code, long_url, created_at, click_count, last_click_at) and endpoints for create, redirect, details and analytics. It adds no NFRs, which is consistent with C-1 and the empty NFR list.

options.name: Python 3.12 + FastAPI + SQLite
pros: Very concise code for four endpoints
cons: Not yet validated end-to-end in the orchestrator pipeline, so the build, test and deploy path carries more risk
FastAPI/Pydantic return 422 on validation errors by default. That still satisfies the 4xx in FR-10, but the behavior needs care.
The TestClient follows redirects by default, so tests must disable this explicitly for AC-2.1 and AC-3.1
options.fit: Functionally adequate for FR-1 to FR-15. It is less preferred only because it has not been validated end-to-end.

options.name: Go 1.22 + chi + SQLite
pros: Small, fast binary that starts quickly
net/http gives explicit control over 302 and Location headers (FR-2, FR-3)
cons: Not yet validated end-to-end in the orchestrator pipeline
SQLite drivers either need cgo (mattn) or carry an extra dependency (modernc), which complicates the build
More hand-written boilerplate for JSON handling and validation
options.fit: Functionally adequate for FR-1 to FR-15. It is less preferred because it has not been validated end-to-end and the SQLite driver adds build complexity.

decision.rationale:
The spec has no constraints that mandate a technology and no NFRs (C-1 answered 'none'), so the choice rests on delivery risk and on fit with the functional requirements. java21-springboot3-maven is the only supported stack VALIDATED end-to-end, and it fully covers the MVP scope:
- Create: POST, with service-generated codes (FR-1, FR-8), an independent row per submission (FR-9), and http/https absolute-URL validation that returns 400 (FR-10).
- Redirect: GET, returning 302 with a Location header (FR-2, FR-3). An atomic SQL UPDATE increments click_count and sets last_click_at only on a successful redirect (FR-5, FR-6, FR-14).
- Details: GET, returning code, longUrl and createdAt (FR-4, FR-11).
- Analytics: a separate GET returning clickCount and lastClickAt, where lastClickAt is null when the link has never been clicked (FR-7, FR-13).
- Errors and access: 404 for unknown codes on redirect, details and analytics (FR-12), and no authentication layer (FR-15).
SQLite is the stack's datastore and is enough to persist links and counters.
consequences: Persistence is a single SQLite table, short_link(code PK, long_url, created_at, click_count default 0, last_click_at nullable), which traces to FR-1, FR-5, FR-6, FR-9, FR-11 and FR-13.
Click counting uses one atomic UPDATE statement per successful redirect, so no click is lost or double-counted. Unknown codes never touch any row (FR-14, AC-14.2).
Short codes are random, service-generated strings, and a uniqueness check retries on collision (FR-8, FR-9).
Spring Security, rate limiting, problem+json validation and Prometheus metrics are not included. No NFR was selected (C-1), and authentication is out of scope (FR-15).
The service exposes no update, delete, expiration, custom alias or UI endpoints, in line with the out_of_scope list.
Tests are HTTP-level JUnit 5 / Spring Boot tests with redirect following disabled, one or more per acceptance criterion from AC-1.1 to AC-15.1.
The service accepts JVM startup time and footprint as costs, since the spec sets no performance NFR.
rejected_alternatives: python312-fastapi: functionally suitable and concise, but not yet validated end-to-end in the orchestrator, and the spec has no constraint requiring Python. Its default 422 validation responses and redirect-following test client would also need extra care.
go122-chi: functionally suitable and lightweight, but not yet validated end-to-end. The SQLite driver choice (cgo or a pure-Go driver) adds build risk, and the spec has no constraint requiring Go.

Non-supported options such as Node.js/Express or a Redis-backed counter store were considered for comparison only. They cannot be selected because they are not in supported_stacks, and Redis would also add infrastructure that no requirement asks for.
